slides.question: What is this, in plain words?
slides.notes:
Say: Kestrel Health sells employers fast physiotherapy for their staff, booked into the empty weekday slots of independent clinics. We keep 22% of each booking.
Context: GMV is the gross value of bookings before the clinics' share.
Transition: Here is how fast it is growing.

slides.question: Is this working, and how fast?
slides.notes:
Say: Bookings were £1.9M in the third quarter, up 31% on the second. Net revenue was £418k.
Context: GMV is bookings paid through Kestrel before the clinics' share. Q2 grew 23% on Q1, so we do not claim 30% a quarter as a trend. The Q1 and Q2 export figures run above finance and are being reconciled.
Transition: The growth comes from a wait nobody else has fixed.

Say: An employee with a back injury waits about 14 weeks for NHS physiotherapy, by our estimate, and the employer pays for the absence either way. Priya's own team waited while the insurer's fast track took days, not hours.

slides.question: Why does this work now, and why will you be the one to build it?
slides.notes:
Say: Private physiotherapy is thousands of small clinics with empty weekday slots and no aggregator. We fill slots they could not fill otherwise, so they accept 22%.
Context: The network is not exclusive and never will be. We win only while we are a clinic's best channel.
Transition: Now the proof.

slides.question: Is the network growing on both sides?
slides.notes:
Say: We added 16 employers in eleven months and ended September with 41 employers, 312 clinics and 71,400 covered employees.
Context: Active means at least one booking in the period. Clinic supply is no longer the constraint in the big cities; it is still thin in the South West and Scotland.

slides.question: Does a real customer get the value you claim?
slides.notes:
Say: At one logistics employer, the 212 employees who used Kestrel recorded 936 MSK sick days in six months, against 1,418 in the same months a year earlier.
Context: Single employer, no control group, self-selected participants, and the employer changed shift patterns in March 2026. Regression to the mean is likely. We do not present this as a general result.
Transition: That difference in what the buyer wants is the heart of the company.
Time: 75

slides.notes:
Say: Insurers optimise for claims cost. Employers optimise for people being at work. Those are different products, and in the UK the employer is the right buyer.

slides.question: Who pays, how much, and does a pound in produce more than a pound out?
slides.notes:
Say: We keep 22% of each booking. Gross margin on that is 61% after clinical operations, payment processing and the triage team. Net revenue annualises to £1.67M.
Context: Blended payback is 9 months against a target of 6; it crept up as enterprise cycles lengthened and two new sales hires ramped. Gross retention is not measured yet.
Transition: Retention depends on who the employer is.
Time: 75

slides.question: Is it one kind of customer or many, and do they stay?
slides.notes:
Say: We lost 7 employers in 12 months, all under 200 employees. None of our 14 enterprise employers has left in two years, and employers as a group spent 118% of the year before.
Context: 14 accounts over two years is a small sample. Enterprise means 250 or more staff on an annual contract. Gross retention is not measured yet.
Transition: So how many such employers are there?

points: Employees at 250+ employers in the UK, Netherlands and Ireland. 18% report an MSK problem in a year; fewer seek treatment, so the real figure is lower.
£403 is the market average spend per case, at 6.2 sessions. Booking value, not Kestrel revenue. Public sources for the three inputs are being added.
slides.question: How big can this get, and how do you know?
slides.notes:
Say: Employees at large employers in three countries, times the share with an MSK problem, times the spend per case: £1.1B of bookings a year, of which our 22% would be £242M.
Context: Physiotherapy pathway only, no prevention or occupational health layers. Our own cases average slightly less than the market spend per case.
Transition: Here is how we reach those employers.
